39 The isotope fluorine-18,
F,
18
9
undergoes + decay to form a stable isotope.
How many neutrons are there in a nucleus of the stable isotope?
A
7
B
8
C
9
D
10

hints: Read the nuclide notation $^{18}_{9}\text{F}$ to get the starting nucleon number $A = 18$ and proton number $Z = 9$.
Recall that in $\beta^+$ decay a proton becomes a neutron, so $A$ stays the same while $Z$ decreases by 1.
Calculate neutrons in the daughter using $N = A - Z$ with the new $Z$ value.
walkthrough: Identify the parent from $^{18}_{9}\text{F}$: nucleon number $A = 18$ and proton number $Z = 9$, so starting neutrons $= 9$.
State the $\beta^+$ rule: $p \rightarrow n + e^+ + \nu_e$, so proton number decreases by 1 and nucleon number is unchanged.
Apply it: daughter has $A = 18$ and $Z = 9 - 1 = 8$, which is an isotope of oxygen.

A.explanation: 7 would be $18 - 11$, which confuses proton and neutron numbers and does not follow $\beta^+$ decay.

B.explanation: 8 is the proton number of the daughter nucleus, not the neutron number $A - Z$.

C.explanation: 9 is the neutron number of the parent $^{18}_{9}\text{F}$, before a proton changes to a neutron.

D.explanation: After $\beta^+$ decay $Z$ falls to 8 with $A$ unchanged at 18, so neutrons $= 18 - 8 = 10$.
